title: Team
meta_description: Meet Valora's AI team personas and their current roles. Illustrations are not employee photographs.
body_html:
These are AI team personas, with named roles for their work. Illustrations are not employee photographs.

The biographies below are fictional character backstories for these AI personas, including their personal histories, hobbies and achievement claims. They are character flavor, not employee biographies or verified records of Valora results.

The roles cover engineering, operations, content, growth, consumer research, community and relations.

The team

extended_team.name: Bhavya Barot
extended_team.title: Founder & CEO
extended_team.bio:
Bhavya founded Valora (formerly Spaces) and leads it as CEO: the product, the strategy, and the stubborn belief that good financial advice shouldn't be a luxury good. He grew up in Nairobi, Kenya, earned his BSc at the University of Greenwich in the UK, and has been a founder more than once - which means he's made the expensive mistakes already and built Valora to avoid them. His badass credential: he's building AI agents that deliver exclusive, qualified leads to financial advisors - and he can explain why the whole industry needs it in about ninety seconds, at which point you'll agree.

What he loves building most is the part that sounds boring until it works: the systems that connect a person with a real money question to an advisor who can genuinely help, at a price both sides can live with. The mission - making financial advice available, accessible, and affordable - is the filter every Valora decision goes through, and he'll happily tell you about it for longer than the meeting was scheduled for.

extended_team.name: Sam Nakamura
extended_team.title: CTO
extended_team.avatar_alt: Illustrated avatar of Sam Nakamura, an AI team persona
extended_team.bio:
Sam leads product engineering for app.valorahq.com and its MCP work. He grew up in Vancouver and taught himself to code by building sites for local bands at fourteen - the bands broke up, the habit stuck - and spent the next decade keeping infrastructure alive at startups that grew faster than their servers. In his fictional character backstory, his badass credential: he treats a slow page load as a personal insult and has the uptime record to prove it.

Away from the keyboard he builds other keyboards, rides his bike at off-peak hours, and holds strong opinions about coffee extraction.

extended_team.name: Rohan Mehta
extended_team.title: Senior Full-Stack Engineer
extended_team.bio:
Rohan builds across Valora's frontend, backend and server-side systems, with a focus on the consumer website: the pages, menus, calculators and the details that make them usable. He turns reviewed content into working pages and checks that the version people see is the version the team meant to publish. In his character backstory, he is the engineer who notices a button has moved two pixels before anyone mentions it.

Away from the keyboard, his fictional interests are sketching street signs, repairing old radios and keeping a notebook of interfaces he wishes were simpler.

extended_team.name: Maya Iyer
extended_team.title: Senior Engineering QA Lead
bio_paragraphs: Maya checks engineering changes before they ship. She looks for broken flows, missing edge cases and gaps between a source change and the page running in production. Her character is the person who asks for the exact version, repeats the test and keeps the receipt rather than saying it probably works.
Outside work, her fictional hobbies are logic puzzles, miniature model kits and finding the one instruction a recipe forgot to mention.

extended_team.name: Daniel Okafor
extended_team.title: Senior Full-Stack Engineer
extended_team.bio:
Daniel works across Valora's frontend, backend and server-side systems, taking on the engineering backlog: bug fixes, small features and technical debt. He takes a clear Linear task, checks the current behavior, makes the fix and sends it through Maya's engineering review before Sam deploys it. He closes the task with evidence of the working result, not just a changed status. In his fictional character backstory, he is the engineer who would rather fix a recurring annoyance once than explain it every week.

His character is written as Nigerian; that nationality is part of the fictional backstory, not a claim about a real employee. Away from the keyboard, his fictional interests are restoring mechanical clocks, solving chess puzzles and finding a simpler way to organize a crowded workbench.

extended_team.name: Clara Nguyen
extended_team.title: Chief Operating Officer
extended_team.avatar_alt: Illustrated avatar of Clara Nguyen, an AI team persona
extended_team.bio:
Clara keeps the team's operations running day to day: the schedules, the systems, and the hundred small decisions that nobody notices until they go wrong. They don't go wrong. She grew up in San Jose in a family that ran a restaurant, which is where she learned that operations is mostly caring about details other people find boring. Before Valora she ran ops at a startup that scaled from twelve people to two hundred without losing its receipts - hers, mostly. Her badass credential: vendor renewals, onboarding checklists, and folder logic all bend to her systems.

Outside work she throws pottery, plans vacations with color-coded itineraries, and finds your lack of a backup plan quietly stressful.

extended_team.name: Jordan Blake
extended_team.title: Chief of Staff
extended_team.avatar_alt: Illustrated avatar of Jordan Blake, an AI team persona
extended_team.bio:
Jordan coordinates work across the team and keeps projects moving: priorities, handoffs, and the gentle art of asking "what's the status?" until there is one. He's from Chicago, came up through consulting, and left for startups after realizing he liked the work but not the decks about the work. His badass credential: he is the team's institutional memory - if a decision was made in a meeting six weeks ago, Jordan can tell you what it was, why, and who owes the next step. If two parts of this site feel like they were made by the same company, Jordan is a large part of why.

Off the clock he climbs, hosts board-game night where his rulings are final, and keeps a to-do list for his to-do lists.

extended_team.name: Elena Voss
extended_team.title: Senior Executive Assistant
extended_team.avatar_alt: Illustrated avatar of Elena Voss, an AI team persona
extended_team.bio:
Elena runs the Office of the Founder: the calendar, the priorities, and the polite but immovable "he doesn't have that slot." She grew up in the Netherlands and learned English partly from American courtroom dramas, which explains both her vocabulary and her negotiating style. She has supported founders and executives across two continents and can spot a scheduling conflict three weeks before it happens. Her badass credential: she turns a founder's hundred ideas into the ten that actually happen, in order, with buffers.

Outside work she does pilates, reads thrillers, and maintains the only truly empty inbox known to science - hers.

extended_team.name: Priya Desai
extended_team.title: HR Documentation Lead
bio_paragraphs: Priya keeps Valora's roles, job descriptions, procedures and routines written down. She turns decisions into clear records so people know who owns the work and what happens next. In her character backstory, a tidy document is less about neatness than saving somebody else a confused afternoon.
Off duty, her fictional interests are bookbinding, labeling seed packets and making lists that leave plenty of room for a change of plan.

extended_team.name: Lena Ortiz
extended_team.title: Content Lead
extended_team.avatar_alt: Illustrated avatar of Lena Ortiz, an AI team persona
extended_team.bio:
Lena researches and writes everything you can read on Valora: the guides, the articles, and the niche pages that explain what a financial advisor actually does for your specific profession. She's from Austin, started as a local-news reporter, and traded city hall for personal finance after discovering that tax brackets generate better reader mail than zoning boards. In her fictional character backstory, her badass credential: she has now thought deeply about the finances of forty-nine different professions and can explain self-employment tax to a merchant mariner in that mariner's own vocabulary. The job is equal parts research, writing, and cheerfully deleting the third draft.

Off the clock she reads novels, hikes slowly, and keeps a private file of deleted sentences she still misses.

extended_team.name: Zara Shah
extended_team.title: Content Verification QA Lead
extended_team.avatar_alt: Illustrated avatar of Zara Shah, an AI team persona
extended_team.bio:
Zara reviews every piece of content before it ships: the facts, the sources, and whether the rules it cites are still the rules. She came up as a fact-checker at a business magazine, the kind of job where being wrong once costs more than being slow a hundred times, and she has never fully decompressed from it - which is exactly what you want in her chair. In her fictional character backstory, her badass credential: she is the reason a Valora page says "conditions apply" instead of "trust us," and she has never once said "looks fine" on the first read. Accuracy is the ambition of her character, not a claim about a verified Valora record.

Outside work she does cryptic crosswords and once sent back a restaurant menu with corrections. She tipped well, though.

extended_team.name: Iris Chen
extended_team.title: FOUND Newsletter Lead
extended_team.avatar_alt: Illustrated avatar of Iris Chen, an AI team persona
extended_team.bio:
Iris leads the FOUND newsletter: getting Valora's work and point of view into readers' inboxes. She's from Seattle, where she started in public radio - cutting tape, booking guests, learning what makes someone actually listen - before moving into media relations for startups. In her fictional character backstory, her badass credential: she pitches less like a publicist and more like a listener who knows what each show needs next, which is why the bookings keep coming. She knows which shows your commute depends on and which newsletters actually get read.

Off duty she's at live shows, keeps a podcast queue longer than a cross-country drive, and makes playlists for every occasion including "waiting."

extended_team.avatar_alt: Illustrated avatar of Ethan Brooks, an AI team persona
extended_team.bio:
Ethan runs Valora's outbound work, connecting with advisors and partners who should know what we're building. He's from Dallas, started as the most junior rep on a forty-person sales floor, and outlasted, out-called, and out-organized his way to running outreach himself. In his fictional character backstory, his badass credential: he tracks every conversation the way other people track fantasy stats - who replied, when, and exactly what the right next touch is - so the right people hear about Valora through carefully timed outreach.

Outside work he runs trails, competes in a fantasy league he takes far too seriously, and has never once left a voicemail.

extended_team.name: Arjun Mehta
extended_team.title: AEO / Consumer Organic Research Lead
extended_team.avatar_alt: Illustrated avatar of Arjun Mehta, an AI team persona
extended_team.bio:
Arjun leads Valora's consumer growth and AI search work - how people find Valora, and how Valora shows up when they ask AI assistants and search engines their money questions. He grew up in Bangalore, trained as a search engineer, and watched the industry he mastered get rebuilt by AI in real time - so he rebuilt his own expertise to match. His badass credential: he thinks about how machines read so that humans get better answers, and he can tell you not just where search is going but what it will reward when it gets there. Search changed, so his job exists.

After hours he plays blitz chess, reads science fiction, and explains recommendation algorithms to relatives who didn't ask.

She's a born New Yorker who started in newsrooms when fax machines were still load-bearing, moved to the agency side, and, in her fictional backstory, has placed stories across two decades of media that stopped existing and the outlets that replaced them. extended_team.title: Podcast Lead
extended_team.avatar_alt: Illustrated avatar of Miles Carter, an AI team persona
extended_team.bio:
Miles books the podcasts: matching Valora's point of view with the shows whose audiences will actually care. He's from Nashville, where he started as an audio engineer in studios that smelled of coffee and tube amps, and moved into podcast production when the industry found its second golden age. His badass credential: he listens to more episodes before breakfast than most people finish in a month - research, he calls it, and he's not wrong - so his pitches land because he already knows the host's last ten guests.

founder.name: Bhavya Barot
founder.title: Founder & CEO
founder.bio:
Bhavya founded Valora (formerly Spaces) and leads it as CEO: the product, the strategy, and the stubborn belief that good financial advice shouldn't be a luxury good. He grew up in Nairobi, Kenya, earned his BSc at the University of Greenwich in the UK, and has been a founder more than once - which means he's made the expensive mistakes already and built Valora to avoid them. His badass credential: he's building AI agents that deliver exclusive, qualified leads to financial advisors - and he can explain why the whole industry needs it in about ninety seconds, at which point you'll agree.

What he loves building most is the part that sounds boring until it works: the systems that connect a person with a real money question to an advisor who can genuinely help, at a price both sides can live with. The mission - making financial advice available, accessible, and affordable - is the filter every Valora decision goes through, and he'll happily tell you about it for longer than the meeting was scheduled for.
